facts: INSPIRE Index Polygons contain locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
The INSPIRE ID relates to a registered title.
The Find a Property service can use an INSPIRE ID to obtain the title registration and plan.
INSPIRE is a subset of HM Land Registry Index Polygons.
The published polygon shows position and indicative extent, not a determined legal boundary.
guards: Require INSPIRE ID provenance before candidate promotion.
Do not treat INSPIRE ID alone as exact-boundary evidence.
Do not infer title number where the INSPIRE-ID linkage has not been read back.
Keep candidate status fail-closed when title registration cannot be resolved.
Record source publication/version with every INSPIRE candidate.
Preserve NO_DATA rather than invent a title or boundary match.

facts: INSPIRE files are divided by local authority area.
A polygon on a local-authority boundary can appear in both authority files.
The dataset covers registered freehold property rather than all possible interests.
Local-authority file identity is delivery metadata, not title identity.
Duplicate delivery records can therefore represent one spatial object.
Deduplication must use stable polygon/INSPIRE identity rather than file occurrence.
guards: Deduplicate cross-authority occurrences before counting candidates.
Do not count the same INSPIRE ID twice when present in two authority files.
Do not use local-authority filename as parcel identity.
Require geometry and INSPIRE-ID consistency across duplicate occurrences.
Flag conflicting duplicate geometry for manual evidence review, not averaging.
Keep candidate counts based on unique verified identities only.

facts: HM Land Registry INSPIRE data is captured against British National Grid.
British National Grid is EPSG:27700.
Each polygon point is represented by X and Y values in the National Grid.
Web-map use commonly requires reprojection to another CRS.
HM Land Registry warns BNG-to-WGS84 style reprojection can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
Native-grid coordinates avoid that web-display reprojection error for spatial matching.
guards: Perform boundary/raster matching in EPSG:27700 where possible.
Never derive exact-boundary evidence from web-map pixel alignment.
Record any CRS transformation applied to a candidate.
Reject unlabelled WGS84 coordinates as exact HMLR geometry evidence.
Do not mix transformed display geometry with native raster sampling coordinates.
Treat up-to-15m reprojection risk as disqualifying for exact-boundary promotion unless controlled.

facts: The current INSPIRE files were published on 5 July 2026.
New files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
Files are available until the next update replaces them.
Downloads are organised by local authority.
Use requires acceptance of Open Government Licence conditions.
A GIS is required to inspect the GML polygons directly.
guards: Record the 5 July 2026 release date for this candidate batch.
Do not silently combine polygons from different monthly releases.
Revalidate release date before a later runtime measurement.
Keep release provenance alongside any selected candidate geometry.
Do not treat file download date as polygon legal-boundary date.
Fail closed when monthly release provenance is unknown.

facts: Practice Guide 10 was updated on 20 July 2026.
HM Land Registry's index map is based on Ordnance Survey mapping.
Spatial data can help identify land for an index-map search.
HM Land Registry accepts ESRI shapefile, MapInfo MID/MIF and TMF spatial formats for this process.
Polygons must be captured against large-scale Ordnance Survey mapping.
OSGB 1936 British National Grid must be used for compatibility with the mapping system.
guards: Require OSGB36 British National Grid for index-map spatial evidence.
Do not accept arbitrary web-map CRS as equivalent.
Keep spatial-search evidence separate from exact legal-boundary evidence.
Do not promote an indicative polygon because it is accepted for search identification.
Record source guide version 20 July 2026 for this gate.
Reject candidate geometry whose CRS cannot be proven.

facts: The 20 July 2026 update changed practice to reduce rejections caused by shapefile and SIM-plan mismatches.
Where a shapefile is lodged HM Land Registry may process the search on the shapefile alone.
If the land cannot be clearly identified from the shapefile HM Land Registry asks for a compliant plan.
Accurate property identification is required for index-map searching.
New-development mapping may not always be immediately available.
Spatial evidence quality can therefore depend on contemporaneous OS mapping context.
guards: Detect shapefile/plan mismatch rather than choosing one silently.
Do not infer missing new-development geometry from nearby mapped features.
Record whether candidate identification came from polygon, plan or both.
Keep ambiguous extents in NO_DATA/NEEDS_EVIDENCE state.
Do not average conflicting plan and shapefile boundaries.
Require a clear spatial-identification path before raster sampling.

facts: A registered estate boundary is a general boundary unless shown as determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
A determined boundary shows the exact line for register purposes.
HM Land Registry does not resolve a boundary dispute merely by determining a boundary.
The exact line must first be identified from evidence.
The determined-boundary plan is retained for reference.
General title-plan position is not itself exact legal-boundary geometry.
guards: Never promote a normal title-plan red edge to exact geometry.
Require explicit determined-boundary or equivalent surveyed evidence for exact-line status.
Keep general-boundary candidates as discovery-only.
Do not calculate centimetric height differences from general-boundary linework.
Record boundary evidence class on every candidate.
Fail closed when exact-line evidence class is absent.

facts: A determined-boundary plan must identify start, end and turning points.
The plan must show sufficient surrounding detail to identify the general position on OS mapping.
The plan must show orientation such as a north point.
The preferred scale is no smaller than 1:200.
The relationship between boundary and physical features must be described.
Non-National-Grid coordinates shown on the plan must be removed for the determined-boundary submission.
guards: Require start/end/turning-point topology before exact-line sampling.
Require stated scale and orientation in exact-boundary plan evidence.
Reject unlabeled coordinate systems.
Do not infer which side of a wall/fence the legal boundary follows.
Require physical-feature relationship when relevant.
Keep cluttered or contradictory plan evidence out of automatic promotion.

facts: Determined-boundary measurements must be accurate to plus or minus 10mm.
Measurements must be horizontal rather than measured along slope.
Measurements must use at least two defined permanent-feature points.
Reference points should preferably be available from both sides of the boundary.
Permanent features should reasonably remain in position for at least 10 years.
Features subject to natural growth or decay are not acceptable measurement controls.
guards: Reject slope-distance measurements unless converted/verified as horizontal.
Require at least two suitable permanent controls.
Reject vegetation or decaying features as survey control.
Do not claim better accuracy than the evidence certificate supports.
Preserve survey-control provenance with any numeric result.
Fail closed when measurement-control geometry cannot be reconstructed.

facts: Only National Grid coordinates are accepted for determined-boundary coordinate plans.
National Grid coordinates require absolute accuracy of plus or minus 300mm.
Relative accuracy must be plus or minus 10mm.
Eastings are recorded before northings.
A suitably qualified professional must certify the coordinate accuracy.
A certificate specifying better accuracy is acceptable when supported.
guards: Require explicit National Grid coordinate provenance.
Do not translate web-map coordinate precision into survey accuracy.
Require certification evidence before exact-coordinate promotion.
Keep absolute and relative accuracy as separate fields.
Reject coordinates with unknown axis order or units.
Do not infer survey quality from decimal places alone.

facts: EA LIDAR Time Stamped DTM is survey-specific raster elevation data.
Available resolutions include 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on survey.
DTM processing removes surface objects to model terrain surface.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files.
Heights are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
Metadata catalogues identify survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
guards: Require exact survey metadata match for each sampled raster.
Do not mix survey dates without recording temporal difference.
Do not treat DSM values as DTM ground values.
Record tile identity and product resolution with every sample.
Require Newlyn vertical reference provenance.
Keep sample NO_DATA if transformation/geoid metadata cannot be resolved.

facts: EA ground-truth points are independently surveyed on flat unambiguous surfaces.
Ground-truth points have accuracy of plus or minus 3cm RMSE.
Ground-truth records include survey date, surface type, survey method, transformation and geoidal models.
LIDAR timestamped surveys are compared against ground truth for quality control.
LIDAR surveys must report less than plus or minus 15cm RMSE to pass quality control.
Standard deviation and random error must be below 10cm for the stated quality-control test.
guards: Do not interpret 15cm RMSE as a guaranteed per-pixel maximum error.
Keep ground-truth accuracy distinct from raster sample accuracy.
Record survey QC metadata when available.
Do not report centimetric parcel differences as definitive when below source error budget.
Flag differences comparable to vertical uncertainty as low-confidence/no-promotion.
Require independent evidence before claiming sub-source-accuracy height differences.

facts: EA data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid.
Elevations are recorded above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
EA LIDAR Composite uses OSTN15 transformation.
Time-stamped and point-cloud surveys can use geoid models specific to the survey period.
EA advises using metadata catalogues to determine the specific geoid model.
Surveys after 26 August 2016 use OSGM15 according to the EA projection guidance.
guards: Require horizontal CRS and vertical datum to be explicit together.
Do not subtract heights from mismatched vertical datums.
Record geoid/transformation model for time-stamped samples.
Do not assume all historical surveys used the same geoid model.
Keep transformation lineage in numeric-result provenance.
Reject datum-unknown samples from official height-difference promotion.

facts: OS Terrain 5 grid is supplied at regular 5m post spacing.
Tiles are 5km by 5km.
Raster height values are calculated as a mean across each 5m pixel.
ASCII values represent pixel centres offset 2.5m from tile edges.
Heights are written to the nearest 0.01m in the ASCII grid.
OS Terrain 5 GML geometry uses EPSG:27700.
guards: Do not interpret 0.01m storage precision as 0.01m terrain accuracy.
Do not treat a 5m cell mean as a point survey measurement.
Sample using documented cell-centre/grid semantics.
Record tile and cell position for cross-checks.
Do not interpolate across tile boundaries without explicit method provenance.
Keep OS Terrain 5 as a coarser secondary cross-check when EA higher-resolution DTM is available.

facts: HMLR candidate geometry, EA elevation rasters and OS Terrain products can share British National Grid spatial context.
Their legal meaning, spatial resolution and accuracy classes are different.
INSPIRE supplies indicative property extent rather than exact legal boundary.
EA time-stamped DTM provides survey-specific terrain heights with metadata lineage.
OS Terrain 5 provides a coarser 5m terrain grid suitable for secondary consistency checks.
A defensible height-difference result requires all boundary, CRS, datum, raster-lineage and integrity gates to pass together.
guards: Do not promote numeric results from INSPIRE plus raster overlap alone.
Require exact/reliably surveyed boundary evidence before official parcel-boundary measurement.
Require matching EPSG:27700 or documented transformation.
Require common vertical datum before subtraction.
Require remote runtime and integrity readback before publishing measured rows.
If any gate is missing, preserve NO_DATA rather than infer a height difference.
